correctness.rationale: Multiplicativity gives (p^(2^t)+1)(q+1)=q(p^(2^t)+1+D_t(p)) and reduces equality to p^(2^t)+1=q D_t(p), D_t(b)=sum_(j<t)b^(2^j)-1. For t=1, D=b-1, divisibility iff b-1 divides 2, giving (p,q)=(2,5),(3,5). For t=2, remainder (b-1)^2+1 is strictly between 0 and b^2+b-1. For t>=3 let y=b^(2^(t-2)), u=sum_(j<t-2)b^(2^j)-1; elementary induction gives y>=4 and 1<=u<=y/3. D=y^2+y+u and b^(2^t)+1=y^4+1 has representative R=(y+u)^2+1, with D<R<2D, strictly excluding divisibility for every integer b>=2. Independently tested modular remainders for b=2..49 and t=1..7 plus both actual p2,p3 t1 solutions. Infinite obstruction is from inequalities, not experiments. No claim about nondyadic exponents or >2 prime factors.
